hook: More than half of humanity lives inside this one circle.

beats.narration: More than half of humanity lives inside this one circle.
It's about 3,300 kilometres across from the centre, which sits near Myanmar's border with China.
beats.claim: Half the world's population lives within about 3,300 km of a point near Mong Khet, Myanmar (Quah's calculation); the paper places the centre in northern Yunnan.

beats.narration: It's the smallest circle on Earth that holds half of everyone.
beats.claim: The Valeriepieris circle is the circle of smallest radius containing half the Earth's population.

beats.narration: Delhi, Mumbai, Beijing, Manila and Jakarta are all inside.
beats.claim: Great-circle distances from 21.65N 99.63E: Delhi 2,381 km, Mumbai 2,800, Beijing 2,576, Manila 2,386, Jakarta 3,195; all under 3,300.
Tokyo is about 4,173 km from the same centre, outside a 3,300 km radius.

beats.narration: The reason: northern India, southern China and Southeast Asia together hold half the world's people.
beats.claim: The radius is small because northern India, southern China and south-east Asia together hold half the world population.

beats.narration: So everyone in Europe, Africa, the Americas and Australia is the smaller half. Inside or outside?

title: Half of humanity lives inside this circle
description: The smallest circle containing half the world's population has a radius of only about 3,300 km.
